nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Serves as the chapter roadmap and table of contents for Chapter 14, introducing performance optimization and cost governance across token consumption, inference latency, usage observation, and budget planning.
nodes.languageNotes: Outlines the chapter's four core dimensions: token consumption, inference latency, real-time usage observation, and multi-tier budget governance.

nodes.name: 14.1_token_context_cost.md
nodes.summary: Analyzes the three-stage token lifecycle in agent conversations and details systematic optimization techniques for input and output tokens. Covers system prompt refinement, specialized per-agent tool allocation, dynamic context pruning, and automated transcript compaction.
nodes.languageNotes: Examines token cost acceleration over multi-turn sessions and provides concrete openclaw.json configurations for contextPruning and compaction safeguard policies.

nodes.name: 14.2_latency_throughput.md
nodes.summary: Establishes formal mathematical models for end-to-end latency decomposition across LLM inference, tool I/O, sandbox execution, and orchestration overhead. Formulates a structured multi-component cost equation and contrasts serial versus parallel multi-agent dispatch architectures.
nodes.languageNotes: Breaks down end-to-end request latency into LLM time-to-first-token, tool I/O critical paths, container sandbox lifecycles, and orchestration queue delays.

nodes.name: 14.3_usage_budget.md
nodes.summary: Guides real-time token consumption observation and budget control using OpenClaw built-in commands like /status, /usage cost, and /compact alongside Dashboard metrics. Explains global and per-agent budget quotas, automated session pruning, model tiering fallbacks, and cost anomaly alerts.
nodes.languageNotes: Details operational CLI tools (openclaw gateway usage-cost, /status, /usage cost) and outlines architecture for integrating external billing quotas with Prometheus alerts.

nodes.name: 14.4_budget_templates.md
nodes.summary: Provides detailed monthly cost breakdowns and deployment budget templates across three distinct operating tiers: Personal/Small Team, Medium Scale/Startup, and Enterprise. Features a cost driver weight comparison matrix and a practical budget planning decision tree.
nodes.languageNotes: Analyzes monthly financial models from $39 SaaS hobby projects to $35,000 multi-region hybrid enterprise clusters, detailing LLM token, tool API, storage, and SRE labor ratios.

nodes.name: summary.md
nodes.summary: Summarizes key operational takeaways from Chapter 14, provides a 6-point cost optimization audit checklist, and previews troubleshooting trees and ecosystem integration chapters.
nodes.languageNotes: Includes self-inspection checks for token baselines, prompt trimming, agent tool separation, compaction policies, fallback chains, and weekly cost audits.
